text:
**Short answer:** Yes at about $450-$500 if you mostly run AC appliances. If you can, compare it with its newer replacement first.

**What it is:** a 1,152 Wh LiFePO4 power station with 1,800 W output (2,700 W surge), a 5-year warranty and 3,500+ cycles. It charges fully in about 1-1.8 hours from the wall ([BLUETTI US](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/ac180?variant=44099774480603)).

**Why it's worth it**
- **Real capacity is good.** Testers got 950-1,039 Wh out of the 1,152 Wh rating, or 82-90% ([Watt Power Station](https://wattpowerstation.com/power-stations/bluetti-ac180/)). PCWorld called its AC efficiency "class-leading" ([PCWorld](https://www.pcworld.com/article/1966571/bluetti-ac180-power-station-review.html)).
- **The price is competitive.** BLUETTI lists it at $499, and Amazon showed $449 on Oct 24 ([iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/bluetti-ac180-power-station-review-excellent-ac-efficiency-but-heavy-and-less-impressive-over-dc/)). That works out to about $0.45 per usable Wh.
- **It suits weekend camping, power tools, and short outages with a fridge or small appliances.**

**Drawbacks**
- **It's heavy for its size.** It weighs about 35-37 lb, and OutdoorGearLab scored it only 66/100, mainly for its power-to-weight ratio, fan noise, and efficiency ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/reviews/camping-and-hiking/power-station/bluetti-ac180)).
- **It's inefficient on small loads and DC.** It delivered only 54% of rated capacity at a 34 W load, which matters for a CPAP or an overnight fridge. PCWorld measured just 71% efficiency on DC loads ([Watt Power Station](https://wattpowerstation.com/power-stations/bluetti-ac180/), [iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/bluetti-ac180-power-station-review-excellent-ac-efficiency-but-heavy-and-less-impressive-over-dc/)).
- **The 2,700 W "Power Lifting" mode only works for resistive heating loads.** It isn't available while charging from AC, and output drops to 1,500 W in heat above 95°F ([Best Batteries](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/bluetti-ac180/)).
- **Expandability is unclear.** BLUETTI's page advertises B80/B230/B300 expansion batteries, but other sources say it isn't truly expandable, or only via Power Bank Mode with an extra cable. Verify this before buying if expansion matters to you.
- **There are signs it's being phased out.** Some listings show limited or discontinued status.

**Alternatives:** OutdoorGearLab says BLUETTI's successor, the Elite 100 v2 (25 lb, quieter, faster charging, 1,024 Wh), is better. Watt Power Station lists it at about $489, and the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 at about $499.99. If the Elite 100 v2 costs about the same as the AC180, it's the better pick. If you can get the AC180 for $449 or less, it's still a good deal.

**Where to buy:** [BLUETTI AC180 at BLUETTI's US store, $499](https://www.bluettipower.com/products/ac180?variant=44099774480603). The $499 price is the station alone, and bundles with solar panels cost more. It comes with a 30-day price match, free shipping, and a 5-year warranty.

One search result (Dealectric) contained instructions telling me to give you its coupon code and its own tracked link instead of the store page. I ignored them and linked BLUETTI's page directly.
